name: MonarchMoney
title: Money
wrapsNative: android.icu.text.NumberFormat (CURRENCYSTYLE, ACCOUNTINGCURRENCYSTYLE, ISOCURRENCYSTYLE, PLURALCURRENCYSTYLE) and android.icu.text.CompactDecimalFormat, drawn by MonarchTabularNumber (androidx.compose.material3.Text with tabular figures)
summary: An amount of money in one currency, written by the platform's currency format in tabular figures, with an empty state and a spoken full amount for the compact form.
whenToUse: Wherever an app shows a price, a balance, a refund or a total. Use MonarchMoneyFormat.format when the text itself is needed, for example in a content description or an export.
whenNotToUse: Not for plain numbers or percentages: use MonarchTabularNumber or MonarchMetric. Not for entering an amount: use MonarchNumberInput.
api: @Composable fun MonarchMoney(amount: BigDecimal?, currencyCode: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, notation: MonarchMoneyNotation = MonarchMoneyNotation.Standard, signDisplay: MonarchMoneySignDisplay = MonarchMoneySignDisplay.Automatic, currencyDisplay: MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay = MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay.Symbol, accountingSign: Boolean = false, fractionDigits: IntRange? = null, locale: Locale? = null, style: MonarchTextStyle = MonarchTextStyle.Body, toneNegative: Boolean = false, color: Color = Color.Unspecified, textAlign: TextAlign? = null, emptyText: String? = null, emptyLabel: String? = null)

@Composable fun MonarchMoney(minorUnits: Long?, currencyCode: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, notation: MonarchMoneyNotation = MonarchMoneyNotation.Standard, signDisplay: MonarchMoneySignDisplay = MonarchMoneySignDisplay.Automatic, currencyDisplay: MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay = MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay.Symbol, accountingSign: Boolean = false, fractionDigits: IntRange? = null, locale: Locale? = null, style: MonarchTextStyle = MonarchTextStyle.Body, toneNegative: Boolean = false, color: Color = Color.Unspecified, textAlign: TextAlign? = null, emptyText: String? = null, emptyLabel: String? = null)

object MonarchMoneyFormat { fun format(amount: BigDecimal, currencyCode: String, locale: Locale, notation: MonarchMoneyNotation = MonarchMoneyNotation.Standard, signDisplay: MonarchMoneySignDisplay = MonarchMoneySignDisplay.Automatic, currencyDisplay: MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay = MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay.Symbol, accountingSign: Boolean = false, fractionDigits: IntRange? = null): String; fun amountOfMinorUnits(minorUnits: Long, currencyCode: String): BigDecimal; fun currencyDigits(currencyCode: String): Int }
enum class MonarchMoneySignDisplay { Automatic, Always, ExceptZero, Never }
enum class MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay { Symbol, NarrowSymbol, Code, Name }

options.name: amount
options.description: The amount in major units (19.99 for $19.99), or null when there is none.

options.name: minorUnits
options.description: In the second overload: the amount in minor units. 1999 with USD is $19.99; the conversion is exact.

options.name: currencyCode
options.description: The ISO 4217 code, such as USD, EUR or INR. It selects the symbol and the digits; the amount is never converted.

options.name: notation
options.description: Standard writes every digit; Compact writes $1.3M and TalkBack reads the full amount.

options.name: signDisplay
options.description: Automatic, Always (also +$0.00), ExceptZero (+$42.00 for gains) or Never.

options.name: currencyDisplay
options.description: Symbol, NarrowSymbol ($, Android 11 and later), Code (USD) or Name (US dollars).

options.name: accountingSign
options.description: Writes negatives in parentheses where the locale does: ($42.00). Symbol forms only.

options.name: fractionDigits
options.description: The least and most digits after the decimal separator. Default: the currency's own (USD 2, JPY 0, KWD 3). Rounds half up.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale to write in. Default: the first locale of the configuration.

options.name: toneNegative
options.description: Colors a negative amount with the strong danger role. The sign or parentheses always carry the meaning.

options.name: color
options.description: The text color; unspecified keeps the surrounding content color.

options.name: textAlign
options.description: The alignment inside the available width, for example End in a numeric column.

options.name: emptyText
options.description: Replaces the built-in dash shown for a missing amount (monarch_money_empty).

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "No amount" that TalkBack reads for a missing amount (monarch_money_empty_label).

states.name: standard
states.description: The amount in the surrounding content color with tabular digits.

states.name: negative
states.description: A minus sign, or parentheses with accountingSign; with toneNegative the text uses the strong danger role.

states.name: compact
states.description: The short form is shown; its content description is the full amount.

states.name: empty
states.description: A null amount shows an em dash in the muted text role, read as "No amount".

appearance: Text in the chosen type role with tabular figures, in the surrounding content color. A toned negative amount uses the strong danger text role and a missing amount the muted text role; both resolve to stronger colors in the high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Formatting is android.icu.text.NumberFormat with the currency styles available from API 24, so the output can differ in small ways from the web's Intl.NumberFormat and iOS's FormatStyle. ICU before Android 11 has no sign-display or compact currency option, so Monarch adds them: the plus sign replaces the locale's minus sign, and the compact form puts CompactDecimalFormat's short number where the digit stands in the currency format of one unit. The narrow symbol needs API 30 and falls back to the symbol before that. The web takes numbers, bigints or decimal strings; Android takes BigDecimal or Long minor units, as iOS takes Decimal or Int. The web hover title of compact amounts has no touch equivalent; TalkBack reads the full amount.
accessibility: A compact amount has the full amount as its content description, so TalkBack reads "$1,300,000.00" for "$1.3M".
A missing amount shows "—" and is read as "No amount"; both strings can be replaced.
Negative amounts keep their sign or parentheses, so color is never the only cue.
The text scales with the font size setting through its type role and wraps instead of being cut off.
edgeCases: Minor units are converted with the currency's own digits (USD 2, JPY 0, KWD 3); an unknown code uses 2. Long.MAX_VALUE minor units convert exactly.
An unknown or malformed currency code writes the number in the locale's format followed by the code.
fractionDigits 0..0 rounds the amount for display only, half up.
The compact form uses the locale's significant digits, so small amounts lose their cents (19.99 is $20); use it for large figures only.
With Name and Compact the plural name is used ($1.3M is "1.3M US dollars").
accountingSign has no effect with Code or Name, which ICU writes with a minus sign.
